register.name: New Mexico Compilation Commission - NM OneSource (Current New Mexico Statutes Annotated 1978)
register.access_notes: Partly blocked, then read successfully in a real browser. WebFetch of nmonesource.com returned HTTP 403 for every path tried (/nmos/nmsa/en/index.do, /nmos/nmsa/en/nav_date.do), and a plain curl request 404'd or was refused, so the site does not serve scripted clients. Loading the same URLs in a real browser worked. The site wraps all statute content in an iframe (src '<path>?iframe=true'), so the outer page looks empty to text extraction; appending '?iframe=true' to each item URL returns the chapter table of contents and text. I then read the chapter-by-date navigation (84 chapters over 4 pages) and nine chapter pages, roughly 15 page loads in total, spaced several seconds apart. The Commission's own site www.nmcompcomm.us is reachable by ordinary fetch and supplied the currency statement and copyright notice. No block, challenge or rate limit was circumvented; the 403 for scripted clients is recorded here rather than worked around, and everything below was read through the site's normal browser interface. The URLs given for each Act are the outer (canonical) item URLs; a scripted re-fetch will need the '?iframe=true' form.

licence.summary: Not an open licence. The New Mexico Compilation Commission, a state agency, compiles and publishes NMSA 1978 and asserts all rights reserved over its publications; nothing on nmonesource.com or nmcompcomm.us grants reuse, and nothing grants adaptation. The statutory text itself, however, is a government edict and is not subject to copyright (Georgia v. Public.Resource.Org, 590 U.S. 255 (2020)), so the Commission's assertion can only reach its own additions - the annotations, compiler's notes, case notes, headnotes and the arrangement of the compilation, which are extensive on this site and which an encoding project should not copy. Encoding the operative statutory text is therefore sound; copying NM OneSource's annotations is not. The Commission also sells print and eBook editions, so there is a commercial interest in the compilation even though the publisher is the state agency itself rather than LexisNexis or Thomson Reuters.
licence.attribution: New Mexico Statutes Annotated 1978, New Mexico Compilation Commission, via NM OneSource (nmonesource.com).

acts.title: New Mexico Statutes Annotated 1978, Chapter 50 (Employment Law), Article 4 - Labor Conditions; Payment of Wages (contains the Minimum Wage Act)
acts.verified_how: Fetched the NM OneSource chapter page (item 4420, '?iframe=true' form) in a browser on 23 September 2026: page title 'Chapter 50 - Employment Law - NMOneSource.com'; the item's metadata field reads Collection 'Current New Mexico Statutes Annotated 1978' and the breadcrumb for the collection reads 'Current New Mexico Statutes Annotated 1978 > Date: 2026'; the chapter table of contents lists 'ARTICLE 4 Labor Conditions; Payment of Wages' with no repeal marker, where other articles in the same chapter are expressly marked '(Repealed.)' (e.g. 'ARTICLE 5 Employment of Women (Repealed.)', 'ARTICLE 14A Rapid Workforce Development (Repealed.)'). Currency confirmed separately from the Commission's own site (www.nmcompcomm.us/scope-of-coverage-2/): NMSA 1978 on NM OneSource is current through the Second Session of the Fifty-Seventh Legislature (2026); NM OneSource footer shows 'Website last modified: 09/22/2026'.
acts.notes: Article 4 carries both the wage-payment rules (pay periods, permitted deductions, enforcement by the Labor Relations Division of the Workforce Solutions Department) and the Minimum Wage Act, the short-titled Act within the article. The article-level citation is the form the register itself uses; individual section numbers were not each verified.

acts.title: New Mexico Statutes Annotated 1978, Chapter 50 (Employment Law), Article 17 - Healthy Workplaces (the Healthy Workplaces Act)
acts.verified_how: Same chapter page as above (item 4420, browser, 23 September 2026, collection 'Current New Mexico Statutes Annotated 1978', date 2026): the table of contents lists 'ARTICLE 17 Healthy Workplaces' as the last article of the chapter, with no '(Repealed.)' marker, alongside 'ARTICLE 16 Caregiver Leave'.
acts.notes: This is New Mexico's paid-sick-leave statute (the Healthy Workplaces Act), the state's principal leave entitlement for private-sector employees. Article 16, Caregiver Leave, is a narrower companion. New Mexico has no statutory paid public-holiday entitlement for private employers - holiday pay is contractual - so this Act is the closest match for the topic rather than an exact one.

acts.title: New Mexico Statutes Annotated 1978, Chapter 50 (Employment Law), Article 4 - Labor Conditions; Payment of Wages
acts.verified_how: Same chapter page as above (item 4420, browser, 23 September 2026): 'ARTICLE 4 Labor Conditions; Payment of Wages' present in the table of contents of the current NMSA 1978 collection, not marked repealed.
acts.notes: Listed a second time because it is the same statute serving a second topic. New Mexico is an at-will employment state with no severance-pay statute and no mini-WARN Act, so the only statutory rules on ending employment are the final-wage rules in this article (timing of payment on discharge and on resignation). Entitlement after job loss sits in the Unemployment Compensation Law, NMSA 1978 ch. 51, art. 1 (https://nmonesource.com/nmos/nmsa/en/item/4425/index.do), which I also verified as present and unrepealed; it is recorded here as a cross-reference rather than as this topic's Act.

acts.title: New Mexico Statutes Annotated 1978, Chapter 10 (Public Officers and Employees), Article 11 - Retirement of Public Officers and Employees Generally (the Public Employees Retirement Act)
acts.verified_how: Fetched the NM OneSource chapter page (item 4364, '?iframe=true' form) in a browser on 23 September 2026: page title 'Chapter 10 - Public Officers and Employees - NMOneSource.com', collection 'Current New Mexico Statutes Annotated 1978', date 2026; the table of contents lists 'ARTICLE 11 Retirement of Public Officers and Employees Generally' with no repeal marker, immediately followed by 'ARTICLE 12 Judicial Retirement (Repealed.)' - so repealed articles are marked and this one is not.
acts.notes: Contributory old-age insurance for the general population is federal (Social Security Act, 42 U.S.C. ch. 7), so the in-scope state statute is the public-employee pension scheme: the Public Employees Retirement Act administered by PERA. Related statutes in the same chapter are Article 7A (Deferred Compensation) and Article 7C (Retiree Health Care); the separate Educational Retirement Act sits in ch. 22. New Mexico's other contributory social-insurance statute is the Unemployment Compensation Law, NMSA 1978 ch. 51, art. 1.

acts.title: New Mexico Statutes Annotated 1978, Chapter 27 (Public Assistance), Article 2 - Public Assistance Act
acts.verified_how: Fetched the NM OneSource chapter page (item 4358, '?iframe=true' form) in a browser on 23 September 2026: page title 'Chapter 27 - Public Assistance - NMOneSource.com', collection 'Current New Mexico Statutes Annotated 1978', date 2026; the table of contents lists 'ARTICLE 2 Public Assistance Act' with no repeal marker, in a chapter where repealed articles are marked (e.g. 'ARTICLE 12 Child Health (Repealed.)').
acts.notes: The Public Assistance Act is the framework statute for state-administered assistance and Medicaid. The closely related Article 2B is the New Mexico Works Act (the TANF programme), and Article 6 covers utility supplements and assistance; both remain in force and are cross-references rather than competing choices for this topic.

acts.title: New Mexico Statutes Annotated 1978, Chapter 7 (Taxation), Article 2 - Income Tax General Provisions (the Income Tax Act)
acts.verified_how: Fetched the NM OneSource chapter page (item 4340, '?iframe=true' form) in a browser on 23 September 2026: page title 'Chapter 7 - Taxation - NMOneSource.com', collection 'Current New Mexico Statutes Annotated 1978', date 2026; the table of contents lists 'ARTICLE 2 Income Tax General Provisions' and 'ARTICLE 3 Income Tax Withholding', neither marked repealed, in a chapter where many articles are expressly marked '(Repealed.)' (e.g. 'ARTICLE 6 Banking and Financial Corporations Tax (Repealed.)').
acts.notes: Article 2 is the Income Tax Act (personal income tax). Employer withholding is the immediately adjacent Article 3, Income Tax Withholding (the Withholding Tax Act), verified on the same page and also in force; administration and assessment sit in Article 1 (the Tax Administration Act). Article 2 is recorded as the principal statute for the topic with Article 3 as its withholding companion.

acts.title: New Mexico Statutes Annotated 1978, Chapter 59A - New Mexico Insurance Code
acts.verified_how: Fetched the NM OneSource chapter page (item 4438, '?iframe=true' form) in a browser on 23 September 2026: page title 'Chapter 59A - Insurance Code - NMOneSource.com', collection 'Current New Mexico Statutes Annotated 1978', date 2026; the table of contents opens with 'ARTICLE 1 Insurance Code' and includes 'ARTICLE 16 Trade Practices and Frauds' and 'ARTICLE 18 The Insurance Contract', none marked repealed. The superseded chapter is separately listed in the collection as 'Chapter 59 - Insurance [Repealed.]', confirming 59A is the live code.
acts.notes: Claim handling is governed within the Insurance Code: Article 16 contains the unfair claims practices provisions (the Trade Practices and Frauds article, source of New Mexico's statutory bad-faith claim) and Article 18 the general insurance-contract rules. Chapter 59A is recorded as the principal consolidated statute because the Code is a single enacted code rather than a set of separate Acts.

acts.title: New Mexico Statutes Annotated 1978, Chapter 62 (Electric, Gas and Water Utilities) - Public Utility Act
acts.identifier: NMSA 1978, ch. 62, arts. 3 to 6 and 8 to 13 (Public Utility Act)
acts.verified_how: Fetched the NM OneSource chapter page (item 4407, '?iframe=true' form) in a browser on 23 September 2026: page title 'Chapter 62 - Electric, Gas and Water Utilities - NMOneSource.com', collection 'Current New Mexico Statutes Annotated 1978', date 2026; the table of contents lists 'ARTICLE 3 Public Utility Act; Preamble and Definitions', 'ARTICLE 6 Powers and Duties of Commission', 'ARTICLE 8 Duties and Restrictions Imposed Upon Public Utilities' and 'ARTICLE 13 Public Utility Act Miscellaneous Provisions', none marked repealed, while 'ARTICLE 3A Electric Utility Industry Restructuring Act of 1999 (Repealed.)', 'ARTICLE 5 New Mexico Public Utility Commission (Repealed.)' and 'ARTICLE 7 Natural Gas Price Protection (Repealed.)' are marked repealed.
acts.notes: The Public Utility Act is spread across several articles of chapter 62 rather than sitting in one; rates, charges, billing and service obligations are in Articles 6, 8 and 13, and the regulator is the Public Regulation Commission (Article 19). Consumer billing detail is largely in PRC rules (NMAC title 17) made under this Act rather than in the statute.

acts.title: New Mexico Statutes Annotated 1978, Chapter 47 (Property Law), Article 8 - Owner-Resident Relations (the Uniform Owner-Resident Relations Act)
acts.verified_how: Fetched the NM OneSource chapter page (item 4408, '?iframe=true' form) in a browser on 23 September 2026: page title 'Chapter 47 - Property Law - NMOneSource.com', collection 'Current New Mexico Statutes Annotated 1978', date 2026; the table of contents lists 'ARTICLE 8 Owner-Resident Relations' and 'ARTICLE 8A Rent Control Prohibition' with no repeal markers, in a chapter where recompiled and repealed articles are marked (e.g. 'ARTICLE 7E Homeowner Association (Recompiled.)').
acts.notes: This is New Mexico's residential landlord and tenant statute (the Uniform Owner-Resident Relations Act). The consumer half of the topic is the Unfair Practices Act at NMSA 1978 ch. 57, art. 12 ('ARTICLE 12 Unfair Trade Practices', verified as present and unrepealed on https://nmonesource.com/nmos/nmsa/en/item/4423/index.do on the same date); because only one statute may be recorded per topic, the tenancy Act is recorded and the Unfair Practices Act noted here. Mobile-home tenancies sit separately in ch. 47, art. 10.

topic_gaps.reason: No New Mexico statute. Air-passenger compensation and denied-boarding rules are federal (49 U.S.C. 41712; 14 C.F.R. pt. 250), and state regulation of an air carrier's prices, routes or services is expressly preempted by 49 U.S.C. 41713. New Mexico's transport chapters cover motor carriers (NMSA 1978 ch. 65) and aeronautics (ch. 64) as licensing and safety matters, with no passenger compensation scheme.
Federal matter. Customs duties are exclusively federal (U.S. Const. art. I, sec. 8, cl. 1 and sec. 10, cl. 2; Tariff Act of 1930, 19 U.S.C.). No state statute exists or could exist.
